title: Presentation-compatible fundamental class for a flat lci curve
statement: Let $S$ be a Noetherian scheme, meaning locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme], and let $f:X\to S$ be flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and finitely presented (locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], quasi-compact [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] and quasi-separated [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism]), with nonempty geometric fibres pure of dimension one [def-weil-geometric-fibre, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Assume $X$ is covered by regular affine curve presentations: affine opens $U=\operatorname{Spec}B\subset X$ above $V=\operatorname{Spec}R\subset S$, with an $R$-algebra isomorphism $B=R[x_0,\ldots,x_c]/(f_1,\ldots,f_c)$ whose ordered relations $f_1,\ldots,f_c$ form a regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence] in $R[x_0,\ldots,x_c]$. Let $K_{X/S}$ be the adjunction line, with its canonical presentation comparisons, of [lem-trf-flat-lci-canonical-adjunction]. There is a morphism $\alpha:\Omega^1_{X/S}\to K_{X/S}$ of $\mathcal O_X$-modules, where differentials are [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials], with the following formula in every regular affine curve presentation as above (whether or not it belongs to the given cover). Let $e_0:\Gamma(U,K_{X/S})\simeq B$ be the trivialization of the adjunction line of this presentation given by the basis $(\bar f_1\wedge\cdots\wedge\bar f_c)^\vee\otimes(dx_0\wedge\cdots\wedge dx_c)$. There is a sign $\epsilon_c\in\{1,-1\}$, depending only on $c$ (fixed by the sign conventions of the canonical comparisons of the cited adjunction lemma), such that $e=\epsilon_c e_0$ satisfies $e(\alpha(d\bar a))=\overline{\det(\partial(f_1,\ldots,f_c,a)/\partial(x_0,\ldots,x_c))}$ for every polynomial $a\in R[x_0,\ldots,x_c]$, bars denoting images in $B$. Thus the local maps given by these signed Jacobian formulas agree under the canonical adjunction comparisons, including on arbitrary overlaps, and determine $\alpha$. The map $\alpha$ is an isomorphism exactly on the relative smooth locus [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. The map and these descriptions commute with restriction to open subschemes, isomorphisms of $S$-schemes, and arbitrary base change $S'\to S$, using the canonical base-change comparison for $K$ in the cited adjunction lemma. No properness, nodal hypothesis, marking, positivity, or reconstruction assertion is part of this lemma.

proof.text: On each regular chart apply [lem-sfb-affine-conormal-jacobian-realization]: its conormal complex represents the intrinsic cotangent complex, and its wedge map has the stated augmented Jacobian formula. By [lem-sfb-adjunction-cotangent-determinant-normalization], the exterior-model line is the specified adjunction line, with its determinant comparisons. The relation-first normalization gives $e=e_0$; an equivalent shifted convention is absorbed in the fixed sign $\epsilon_c$.

source.place: Tag 0E9Y (lemma-determinant), displayed wedge formula and omitted well-definedness check; cotangent.tex Tags 08SJ, 08SL, conormal model. Extracts old proof steps 1-3 and local transport in step 7; agent-formulated combined local realization.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-virtual-rank-one-cofactor-descent] to $L_{X/S}$ and the models of step 1. Its overlap equality glues the local maps, works for every further regular presentation, and is natural under restrictions and isomorphisms. Transport $w_L$ from $\det L$ to $K$ by [lem-sfb-adjunction-cotangent-determinant-normalization]. The chart formula from step 1 is therefore the required formula for the resulting $\alpha$. It determines $\alpha$ uniquely since the $d\bar x_j$ generate differentials on each chart.

Agent-formulated sheaf descent of the cofactor naturality statement. Extracts old proof step 4 and the comparison/restriction argument of step 7.

proof.text: On a regular chart $U=\operatorname{Spec}B\to V=\operatorname{Spec}R$, the ring map $R\to B$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-affine-criterion], and the geometric fibres of $U\to V$ are open in those of $X\to S$, hence (when nonempty) pure of dimension one. The stalk of the glued map is, in this chart, the wedge map in [lem-sfb-curve-cofactor-smooth-criterion], followed by an isomorphism of lines. That criterion gives both implications: its invertibility locus is exactly the smooth locus, including the case $c=0$.

source.place: Tag 0E9Z (lemma-fundamental-class-lci), both smooth-locus implications; morphisms.tex Tag 02G1; algebra.tex Tags 00T6, 00T7, 00T8. Extracts old proof steps 5-6, including the explicit zh-1 presentation.

proof.text: Restriction and transport through an $S$-isomorphism carry each regular presentation and its conormal comparison $E\simeq L$, with its degree-zero identification, to the corresponding data of the restricted or transported presentation by [lem-sfb-affine-conormal-jacobian-realization]. Hence restriction and transport preserve the cofactor map by [lem-sfb-virtual-rank-one-cofactor-descent]. The canonical normalized comparisons of [lem-sfb-adjunction-cotangent-determinant-normalization] identify its target with $K$; uniqueness in step 2 gives the corresponding equalities for $\alpha$.

source.place: Tag 0E9Y (lemma-determinant), wedge map; more-algebra.tex Tag 0FJM (lemma-determinant-two-term-complexes), intrinsic good-diagram comparison. Agent-formulated sheaf descent of the cofactor naturality statement. Extracts old proof step 4 and the comparison/restriction argument of step 7.

proof.text: For $S'\to S$, work on affine charts $R\to R'$. The quotient $B$ is $R$-flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-affine-criterion]. Apply [lem-sfb-flat-curve-cofactor-scalar-extension] to identify the pulled-back differential and wedge maps, including their intrinsic determinant comparison. By [lem-sfb-adjunction-cotangent-determinant-normalization] this is the stipulated comparison for $K$. The equality glues over affine charts of $S'$; step 2 compares it with every other presentation. Composition holds by the scalar-extension lemma and the normalization. Neither flatness of $S'\to S$ nor Noetherianity of $S'$ is needed.
